To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the Australian unemployment rate is strongly affected by the world economy; (ii) Australian unemployment is strongly affected by domestic monetary and fiscal policy; (iii) monetary policy is more important than fiscal policy in explaining unemployment; (iv) fiscal policy has been more contractionary than monetary policy in the 1990s; (v) the unemployment rate is strongly related to real wage growth; and (vi) the unemployment rate has a long-term effect on the growth of employment.

(a) Australian macroeconomic policy, particularly monetary policy, has had a significant impact upon Australian unemployment and (b) the Australian macroeconomy is not immune from international influences, and in particular, the international business cycle has a significant influence upon Australian unemployment.

the Australian economy has been subject to excessive volatility in output and employment growth, that this volatility has been exacerbated by the effects of tight monetary and fiscal policies, and that the problem of macroeconomic volatility can be addressed effectively by a combination of better policy design and more effective policy implementation.
